You are making ONE surgical fix in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth engines only, zero API spend. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp on every python call. Files you may change: server/pipeline/angle_render.py, server/pipeline/video_assembly.py (COMMENT ONLY, see below) and tests/test_angle_render.py. Nothing else. Never write renders into episodes/ -- keep every output in YOUR task directory.

MEASURED FINDING (2026-07-24, receipts in /home/ankit114/ringer-work/podcast-full-auto-seg38/seg38-audio-excess-rootcause/): Fred E104's angle_segments gate now clears segment 23 and stops at SEGMENT 38, whose real span is source 1093.5 to 1225.328604 (131.828604s) of episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4. The gate renders it as a single-segment program (crossfade_s=0.0). Measured deltas against the frame-count map (expected = round(map_total*48000)):
  2.5s span:    mux +832,  final +832   OK
  30s span:     mux +768,  final +768   OK
  131.83s span: mux +896,  final +11,136  FAILS certification
  the same 131.83s span rendered as angle 'sbs' instead of 'guest': IDENTICAL +896 / +11,136, so this is NOT about raw cam tracks or sync offsets.
So the mux is right and the CFR clean adds 10,240 samples (213ms) on the long span.

ROOT CAUSE: _build_program_audio_filter (server/pipeline/angle_render.py, around lines 691-748) trims each contribution by exact sample index and then ends it with `asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS`. That moves the first timestamp to zero but PRESERVES the internal timestamp holes inherited from the composite audio. cfr_timeline_clean_cmd (server/pipeline/video_assembly.py around 469-499) then runs `aresample=first_pts=0,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS`, which materializes those holes into real inserted samples during the AAC re-encode. Short spans cross few enough holes to stay inside the padding allowance; the 131.83s span does not. The comment in video_assembly.py asserting that this audio chain 'never inserts or drops samples' is FALSE for discontinuous input and must be corrected.

THE FIX (already proven in a scratch probe: final delta went from +11,136 to +896 with the video frame count unchanged at 3,954):
1. In _build_program_audio_filter, replace the per-contribution `asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS` with `asetpts=N/SR/TB`, which regenerates timestamps from the emitted sample count. Keep the sample-exact atrim start/end arithmetic EXACTLY as it is; only the timestamp expression changes. Update the function's docstring and the nearby comments to state why (PTS-STARTPTS preserved source timestamp holes that the CFR clean turned into 10,240 inserted samples on a 131.8s span).
2. In server/pipeline/video_assembly.py, COMMENT ONLY: correct the claim that `aresample=first_pts=0` never inserts or drops samples. State that it does not warp CONTINUOUS input, but that it materializes holes in a discontinuous timeline, which is why the angle-render audio builder must emit continuous per-contribution timestamps. Do not change that command.
3. Do NOT touch the decoded-sample certification (the 0..1023 invariant), do NOT restore -shortest, and do NOT skip certification for long programs. The certification is what caught this; each of those would re-hide it. Say so explicitly if tempted.

ADD to tests/test_angle_render.py a test named exactly test_program_audio_timestamps_are_continuous_over_a_long_span. Build a SYNTHETIC source long enough to cross the failure regime (at least ~120s, 30fps, continuous 48kHz stereo tone via lavfi -- do not depend on the real episode media, which is not in git; keep the frame size tiny such as 160x90 so it stays fast), render ONE segment spanning most of it through the real render_angle_switch with crossfade_s=0.0, and assert: the render returns its path, and 0 <= decoded_samples - round(map_total*48000) <= 1023 where decoded_samples is the sum of ffprobe frame=nb_samples (this host's ffprobe 7.1.5 has no -count_samples). Also assert the final video packet count still matches round(map_total*30) within one frame, so an audio-timestamp change can never silently move the video timeline. If a synthetic source cannot reproduce the discontinuity regime, say so plainly in your final message and instead assert the emitted filter string uses the continuous-timestamp form, rather than writing a test that passes for the wrong reason.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real output into your final message:
  cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_angle_render.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
plus a REAL render of the segment-38 span [{'start':1093.5,'end':1225.328604,'angle':'sbs'}] off episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4 through render_angle_switch (scratch script and output in YOUR task directory) printing the returned path, map_total, expected samples, decoded samples and the delta. A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty -- the coordinator lands it.
